newsitem.title: NORWAY: SOCCER-ROSENBORG PONDER RANGERS'S DOUBLE OFFER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ROSENBORG PONDER RANGERS'S DOUBLE OFFER.

text.p: Norwegian champions Rosenborg confirmed on Tuesday that Scottish champions Glasgow Rangers had made a bid for defenders Erik Hoftun and Staale Stensaas.
The Norwegian NTB news agency said Rangers had followed up their initial interest in the players with a fax offering a joint fee of 30 million crowns ($4.2 million).
The Rosenborg board said it would rather not sell them "as a package" but club chairman Nils Skutle told NTB: "Today's fax shows that Rangers mean business, but we're not in any hurry."
He would not say if Rangers had sent separate offers for the players or how much they were willing to pay for each player.
Both are under contract to the Trondheim-based club. Hoftun could have moved to Napoli last winter but opted to sign a new three-year deal with Rosenborg.
Rosenborg would probably wait for director Rune Bratseth to return from a week's holiday before any decision was made, Skutle said.
On Monday Rosenborg received an offer from Standard Liege for team captain and midfielder Bent Skammelsrud.
Earlier this season the club sold Steffen Iversen to Tottenham for 2.0 million pounds ($3.2 million) and transferred Bjorn Tore Kvarme to Liverpool for free under the Bosman ruling.
